payload.claim: The commit message `commit_squash` writes for every `package_refusal` unconditionally claims "It was re-verified and reviewed before the refusal" (same claim repeated in the docstring at line 319). But `package()`'s refusal paths for a gone parent (line ~712-723), a merge conflict (line ~759-772), a credential in the patch (line 791-792) and a credential in the commit subjects (line 796-799) all return *before* `reverify()` is ever called (line 835). For those four of the seven refusal reasons, re-verification never ran, so the permanent git commit history asserts something false. Only the new-failures, credential-in-body and branch-moved refusals occur after `reverify()`. No test checks this claim against the specific refusal reason, so the gates cannot catch it.
